translations.text: sorrow, many and various, comes into the joy of men.
One man disparages another behind his back with malice and with slanderous words. He speaks fairly to his face, and yet he keeps that deceit in his heart, an unclean hoard.
Then the Lord of hosts will be witness to that sin.
Therefore the prophet said: "Lord of hosts, do not hand me over together with the sinful to destruction in torments, and do not let me be lost in life along with the liars,
those who have very smooth speech and cruel thoughts in the chamber of their spirit, who faithfully promise a pledge with their lips, though their intent does not go that way."
There is woe in the mind, a heart stained with sins, mingled with pain, filled with deceit, even though he shows fair words outwardly.

They are just alike, as the bees carry both together: they bear honourable food, yet have a poisonous tail behind, honey in the mouth, pleasant food. At times they wound sorely with the sting, when the moment comes.
So too are the false men, those who promise faithfulness with their tongue in fair words but think deceitfully, when at the last they cruelly betray,
such a one has the taste of honey in his promises, smooth words of peace, and within his heart, through the devil's craft, a hidden wound.

So this world is now mingled with wickedness; it wanes and waxes. The old one is watchful; day and night he leads astray and troubles mercy with wickedness. He trusts in his might, persecutes the devout, and sows malice and enmity in abundance.
No one loves another in his heart, except for a very few, so that he truly keeps peace and spiritual love, as God commanded him.
Therefore the one who is not wise, prudent, and skilful in the counsel of the soul sets his hope wholly on the pleasant world.

Now that we know the remedy, let us set our minds and our hopes on what is better, so that we may possess the light of heaven above with the angels, as a help to our souls, when God chooses to bring about the end of earthly life!
